title: U.S. House · Georgia's 9th District
area: Northeast Georgia, including Gainesville, Dahlonega, and Toccoa.

context.text: Cook Political Report rates this race Solid Republican; Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball also rate it Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Andrew Clyde
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary over Sam Couvillon and Gregg Poole, 76.0%

summary.text: Andrew Clyde is the Republican incumbent in Georgia's 9th Congressional District, which he has represented since January 2021. A Navy veteran of 28 years, he founded the firearms retailer Clyde Armory in Athens before entering politics. He serves on the House Appropriations and Budget Committees and is seeking another term.

background.text: Born November 22, 1963, according to Wikipedia, which lists his birthplace as Walkerton, Ontario, Canada and says he grew up in Indiana and New York.

Earned his commission from the University of Notre Dame and served as a U.S. Navy officer for 28 years, including three combat deployments to Kuwait and Iraq, according to his official House biography.
After his discharge, settled in Athens, Georgia, and earned a master's degree in corporate finance and entrepreneurship from the University of Georgia.
Established Clyde Armory in 1991 and, according to his official biography, grew it into a nationwide firearms business that now operates two retail locations in Georgia.

Ran in 2020 for the open 9th District seat after Doug Collins did not seek re-election; he won the August 11 Republican primary runoff over state Rep. Matt Gurtler and defeated Democrat Devin Pandy in the November general election.

First elected in November 2020 and took office January 3, 2021. In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the House Appropriations Committee (Subcommittees on Commerce-Justice-Science and on Labor-HHS-Education) and the House Budget Committee.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Jennifer, live in Jackson County, Georgia.

priorities.text: National security, saying China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea remain the greatest foreign threats and that the armed forces need the tools and resources to protect the nation.
Veterans' issues, saying the country must uphold the promises made to service members and eliminate barriers to their education and employment benefits.
Reducing the federal government's footprint on small businesses, citing his own experience as a small business owner and his role on the House Committee on Oversight and Reform.

positions.summary: Says life begins at conception and abortions should be abolished entirely except when the mother's life is at risk; opposes any taxpayer funding of abortion.
positions.quote: I believe that life begins at the moment of conception, and thus, abortions should be abolished entirely, except in the rare instances when the life of the mother is at risk.

positions.summary: Says he will oppose all bills and efforts that seek to limit or restrict Second Amendment rights, and will work to roll back existing firearms restrictions.
positions.quote: I will always be a stalwart defender of the Second Amendment while serving in Congress. Accordingly, I will oppose all bills and efforts that seek to limit or restrict this right in any way, no matter the circumstances.

record.text: Sits on the House Committee on Appropriations and the House Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Caitlyn Gegen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary over Nick Alex, 60.0%

summary.text: Caitlyn Gegen is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 9th Congressional District. She describes herself as a community organizer with experience in local government, raised by public-school-teacher parents, and a University of Georgia graduate who also studied at the London School of Economics. She won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary and says she is running on protecting human rights, affordable living, and universal healthcare.

background.text: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, says her parents were public school teachers and that her sister is a labor and delivery nurse in Georgia.
Says she grew up performing active-shooter drills in school.
Describes herself as a "proud Double Dawg" and recipient of Georgia's HOPE Scholarship; Ballotpedia lists a bachelor's degree and a graduate degree from the University of Georgia.
Studied at the London School of Economics and lived in London, which she says gave her experience of a different form of government and social safety net.
Says her experience as a community organizer and in local government has prepared her to run for Congress; she does not list the specific employers or roles.
Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for the seat, defeating Nick Alex, 60.0% to 40.0%.

priorities.text: Says her sister, a labor and delivery nurse, sees the effects of Georgia's six-week abortion ban, and that this motivates her to work to overturn the Dobbs decision.
Supports "safer gun legislation," citing having grown up doing active-shooter drills in school.
Supports free tuition at public colleges and universities, citing her own experience with the HOPE Scholarship, and "free universal healthcare."

positions.summary: Says she will fight to overturn the Dobbs decision and describes Georgia's six-week abortion ban as hurting women.
Says she will fight for "safer gun legislation" and told Now Georgia people should be trained to own a firearm.
positions.quote: I am going to fight for safer gun legislation

positions.summary: Told Now Georgia she supports abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, arguing its responsibilities could be handled by other federal agencies.
positions.quote: I don't believe ICE serves a unique purpose

positions.summary: Told Now Georgia she wants to restore Affordable Care Act subsidies and move toward Medicare for All; her candidate questionnaire says she will provide Medicare for all.
Her candidate questionnaire says she will fight to increase the minimum wage.
positions.quote: I will fight to increase the minimum wage

positions.summary: Coverage of her campaign launch says she promised to fight for taxing billionaires.
